about.title: Campbell Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Campbell residents rely on countless everyday products — kitchen appliances, tools, vehicle parts, children's items — and most work exactly as expected. But when a product is poorly designed, manufactured with a flaw, or sold without adequate warnings, the results can be serious. Santa Clara County sees a steady mix of household, workplace, and auto-related injuries tied to defective goods, and sorting out who's responsible — the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer — can be complicated without legal guidance. We handle product liability claims for Campbell residents and are familiar with California product liability law. There's no cost for a consultation, no obligation, and we work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless your claim results in a recovery. If a defective product caused you harm, it's worth having our team review what happened and explain your options.

whyChoose.title: Why Product Liability Claims Work Differently in California

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally allows injured people to pursue a claim by showing the product was defective and caused harm, without having to prove the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the path to recovery for someone hurt by a defective product.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Because these claims often hinge on inspecting the defective item itself, keeping it safe and unaltered after an injury can be an important early step.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not usually. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, not that the company was careless. Our team can review your situation and explain how this applies to your case.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury, including packaging, instructions, or parts. This can be important evidence if a claim moves forward. Avoid repairing or discarding it before speaking with us.

Our team is familiar with the area and can help you understand what to expect as your claim moves forward.
